_comment: Shahnama of Firdausi, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. II: Rustam's vengeance in Turan; Gudarz's dream. Paraphrase passages with notes.

title.en: Rustam Reigns Over Turan for Seven Years
title.zh: 魯斯塔姆君臨圖蘭七年

region.en: Thrones of Chin and Sughd (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 秦地與粟特王座（象徵性定位）

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. II, Kai Kaus Part V sec. 11

summary.en: Avenging Siyawush, the elephantine hero marches toward Chin, subdues Khata, Khutan, and all the coasts of Chin, and takes the throne of him whose fortune had come to dust. He gives the ivory throne and the government of Chach to Tus: offend not the offenceless, and practise all humanity and justice, for this world is a lodging not a home. To Gudarz, lord of Sughd and Sipanjab: worth is better than high lineage. Then all the folk of Chin bring handsel: we are thy servants and thy slaves; and Rustam occupies himself for many a day with hawk and cheetah.
summary.zh: 為西亞瓦什復仇，英雄進軍秦地，平定赫塔、忽檀與秦地沿海，取其王座。他把象牙寶座與「恰奇」的治權交給圖斯：「勿欺無辜；當行仁義——此世乃客舍，非家園。」對粟特與西帕恩賈布之主古達爾茲說：「德行重於門第。」秦地百姓獻寶歸附：「我們唯您之命是從。」魯斯塔姆則以鷹獵消磨歲月。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; Rustam's regency in the conquered east. No living community restriction.

passages.text: The chief, the elephantine hero, marched toward the realm of Chin, and with his sword-arm subdued Khata, Khutan, and all the coasts of Chin, and took the throne of him whose fortune had come to dust. This saw spake Rustam first: the man of worth will seek the enemy; 'tis good to slay him if he countereth thee, and good too if he shun the fight and flee.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Kai Kaus Part V sec. 11 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: He gave torques, armlets, and the ivory throne to Tus, besides the government of Chach, and said: if anybody shall revolt, or even call Afrasiyab to mind, cut off his head; but like a father keep from want and travail the wise and peaceful, shunners of the Faith of Ahriman. Offend not the offenceless, and practise all humanity and justice, for this world is a lodging not a home. None ever had more Grace than had Jamshid, yet still high heaven trod him under foot.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Kai Kaus Part V sec. 11 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: To Gudarz he gave a crown of royal gems, with earrings, torque, and throne, and made him lord of Sughd and Sipanjab: worth is better than high lineage, though lineage assisteth men of worth. The tidings spread through Chin that Rustam sat enthroned as over-lord; then all the folk brought handsel of dinars and royal gems and said: we are thy servants and thy slaves; we only tread the earth to do thy bidding. The chieftain gave them quarter for their lives, perceiving that they had discerning minds, and occupied himself for many a day with hawk and cheetah.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Kai Kaus Part V sec. 11 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

title.en: Zawara's Oath and the Harrying of Turan
title.zh: 扎瓦拉之誓與圖蘭浩劫

region.zh: 西亞瓦什獵場（象徵性定位）

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. II, Kai Kaus Part V secs. 12-13

summary.en: Zawara rides to hunt, and a careless Turkman guide points out the forest: this was the hunting-ground of Siyawush, where was he wont to be both glad and merry. The hawk falls from his hand; his lashes run tears of blood; his comrades fell the guide to the ground, and Zawara swears: I will not hunt or sleep or cease from vengeance on Afrasiyab. Roused by Zawara's words the matchless Rustam begins to ravage and to massacre till all the land shows signs of misery; over a thousand leagues the reek of burning rose, till all of noble race come with dust upon their heads protesting: we are aweary of Afrasiyab; shed not, provoking God, more guiltless blood.
summary.zh: 扎瓦拉行獵，粗心的突厥嚮導隨口道：「這便是西亞瓦什的獵場。」他手中鷹落、雙目泣血；部下打倒嚮導，扎瓦拉立誓：「不獵不眠，不誅阿弗拉西亞卜誓不休！」魯斯塔姆受激，縱兵屠戮，千里焦土；貴族們頂土求饒：「我們早恨透了阿弗拉西亞卜；請勿再無端流血。」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: Now as it chanced one day Zawara went to hunt the onager. He rode apace conducted by a Turkman. On the open he saw a forest which, thou wouldest say, one cannot pass, it fresheneth the soul, so many were the scents and tints and streams. The Turkman told Zawara thoughtlessly: this was the hunting-ground of Siyawush, this was his favourite spot in all Turan, where was he wont to be both glad and merry, but elsewhere sad.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Kai Kaus Part V sec. 12 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: A hawk was on his hand; he let it go; the lashes of his eyes ran tears of blood. His comrades of the host approached, observed him in grief and tears; then they began to curse the Turkman guide and felled him to the ground. With gall-drops streaming from his eyes Zawara swore a great oath: I will not hunt or sleep, or cease from vengeance on Afrasiyab; I will not give a moment's rest to Rustam: all must prepare for fight.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Kai Kaus Part V sec. 12 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Roused by Zawara's words the matchless Rustam began to ravage and to massacre till all the land showed signs of misery, and from Turan up to Saklab and Rum folk saw no cultured tract. The Iranians beheaded all the men, both young and old, and made the women and the children slaves. Thus o'er a thousand leagues and more the reek of burning rose. Then all of noble race came with the dust upon their heads protesting: we are aweary of Afrasiyab, and would not see him even in a dream; shed not, provoking God, more guiltless blood.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Kai Kaus Part V sec. 13 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

title.zh: 古達爾茲夢見卡伊霍斯勞

region.zh: 古達爾茲廳堂（象徵性定位）

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. II, Kai Kaus Part V sec. 15

summary.en: Gudarz dreams that a watery cloud, emblem of coming prosperity, rises o'er Iran and on it sits Suriish: there is a youthful prince now in Turan, Shah Kai Khusrau, the offspring of the loins of Siyawush, sprung from Tur upon the mother's side; when his glorious feet shall reach Iran heaven will accord to him his full desire, and he will overturn the sovereignty of Tur — among the chiefs of Iran none will discover him excepting Giv. Gudarz awoke and, with his hoary beard upon the ground, gave thanks to God, and told the dream to Giv in many words.
summary.zh: 古達爾茲夢見一朵雲（雨水之兆）升起於伊朗上空，蘇魯什坐於其上：「圖蘭有位年輕王子——卡伊霍斯勞，西亞瓦什之子，母系出自圖爾；當他的榮光之足踏入伊朗，上天必成全其願，他將推翻圖蘭王權。眾將之中，唯吉夫能尋得他。」老人醒來，以斑白之鬚觸地謝神，將夢境細細說與吉夫。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: Gudarz one night dreamed that a watery cloud rose o'er Iran, and on it sat Suriish, who thus addressed him: give to me thine ear as thou wouldst be released from this distress, from this injurious Turkman dragon-fierce. There is a youthful prince now in Turan, Shah Kai Khusrau by name. He is a prince, the offspring of the loins of Siyawush, a man of worship and of noble race, illustrious, of the stock of Kai Kubad, and sprung from Tur upon the mother's side.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Kai Kaus Part V sec. 15 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Whenas his glorious feet shall reach Iran heaven will accord to him his full desire. Then will he gird him to avenge his father, will overturn the sovereignty of Tur, will make the waters of the Red Sea boil, pause not in vengeance on Afrasiyab, but live in his cuirass the whole year through, and pass his days and nights upon the saddle. Among the chiefs and warriors of Iran none will discover him excepting Giv: such is the outcome destined by the sky. Gudarz awoke and, with his hoary beard upon the ground, gave thanks to God.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Kai Kaus Part V sec. 15 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
